name: Partial duplication of the long arm of chromosome 13 syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Chromosomal microarray and karyotype diagnostic criteria for partial 13q duplication

criteria.description: Detection of partial duplication involving the long arm (q arm) of chromosome 13 by chromosomal microarray or karyotyping
Presence of global developmental delay or intellectual disability
Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphic features such as microcephaly, hypertelorism, and broad nasal bridge
Presence of congenital malformations including cardiac defects or limb anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Confirmed partial duplication of chromosome 13q by genetic testing plus developmental delay or intellectual disability
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies primarily on genetic confirmation; clinical features support but are variable.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Partial duplication of chromosome 13q detected by genetic testing
searchTerms: extra part of chromosome 13 long arm
global delay in growth and skills

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism including hypertelorism and broad nasal bridge
searchTerms: wide-set eyes and broad nose bridge
facial features with hypertelorism and broad nasal bridge
distinct facial shape with spaced eyes and wide nose

common.symptomName: Congenital heart defects (e.g., ventricular septal defect)

occasional.symptomName: Limb anomalies such as clinodactyly or syndactyly
searchTerms: finger abnormalities like clinodactyly or webbing

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric manifestations such as anxiety or behavioral disorders
searchTerms: mental health issues like anxiety or behavior changes

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible metabolic screening abnormalities in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI may show nonspecific findings such as delayed myelination
genetic: Partial duplication of chromosome 13q detected by chromosomal microarray or karyotype
Breakpoint analysis may identify duplicated segments
other: Developmental and neuropsychological assessments confirming intellectual disability

distinguishingFeatures: Full trisomy 13 rather than partial duplication
More severe congenital anomalies including holoprosencephaly
Different spectrum of clinical features and severity
May lack some craniofacial dysmorphisms seen in broader 13q duplications

redFlags: Congenital heart defects causing cyanosis or heart failure
references: Orphanet: Partial duplication of the long arm of chromosome 13 syndrome, ORPHA:262932
Molecular Cytogenetics of Partial 13q Duplications: Clinical and Genetic Correlations, Journal of Medical Genetics, 2022
